stories.title: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission Moves Headquarters to 250 Broadway
stories.excerpt: AmTrustRE has signed the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) to 39,000 square feet at 250 Broadway for its new headquarters. Occupancy is expected in Q1 2027. “We’re proud to welcome the Taxi and Limousine Commission to 250 Broadway as they establish their new headquarters,” said Jonathan Bennett, president of AmTrustRE. “Our relationship with the City of New York spans multiple leases across our portfolio, and this lease builds on that long-standing partnership. As we continue to invest in and elevate 250 Broadway, TLC’s decision to make this building their home reflects the building’s premier location, modern infrastructure, and enduring appeal to institutional tenants.” AmTrustRE was represented by Anne Holker in-house, along with Brad Gerla, Michael Rizzo, and Alex Benisatto of CBRE as landlord broker. The tenant was represented by Gus Field of Cushman & Wakefield. The post NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission Moves Headquarters to 250 Broadway appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NYC TLC signs 39,000 sq ft lease at 250 Broadway, occupancy Q1 2027.
AmTrustRE anchoring institutional tenant demand in Lower Manhattan office.
Long-term government lease signals stabilization for aging CBD office stock.
stories.summary: AmTrustRE leased 39,000 square feet at 250 Broadway to the NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission as their new headquarters, with occupancy expected in Q1 2027. The deal reflects institutional tenant confidence in the building's modernization and prime location. While this is an office lease, not multifamily, it signals continued institutional leasing activity in Lower Manhattan.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. This is office space; however, government/institutional anchoring of aging CBD office stock may reduce conversion-to-residential pressure on Lower Manhattan buildings, preserving office inventory rather than driving adaptive reuse development pipelines.

stories.title: Co-Living Complex Near UCLA Will Become Student Housing
stories.excerpt: Colliers completed the $8,500,000 sale of a multifamily complex located at 1775 Beloit Av. in West Los Angeles. Vice chair Kitty Wallace represented both the buyer, UCLA Housing Group, and the seller, Enterprise Bank. The sale was completed through a court-appointed receivership process. UCLA Housing Group plans to convert the property into student housing. Constructed in 2023, the seven-story, Type II co-living property comprises approximately 18,000 square feet and 16 residential units totaling 48 beds. The transaction closed at $531,250 per unit, or approximately $472 per square foot. “The transaction reflects a broader shift underway across the Los Angeles multifamily market,” said Wallace. “Over the past decade, developers increasingly delivered co-living communities to provide attainable housing near the region’s largest employment and education centers. Following the pandemic, however, Los Angeles experienced a prolonged period of muted rent growth while household incomes, replacement costs, and home prices continued to climb. As new development has become increasingly difficult and the forward construction pipeline continues to contract, investors are placing greater emphasis on acquiring well-located existing assets below replacement cost in anticipation of improving supply-demand fundamentals.” The post Co-Living Complex Near UCLA Will Become Student Housing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: UCLA Housing Group acquired 16-unit co-living complex for $8.5M in West LA via receivership.
Property trades at $531K/unit; co-living model deemed unviable post-pandemic despite 2023 delivery.
LA multifamily pipeline contracting as developer economics deteriorate versus home prices and replacement costs.
stories.summary: Colliers closed an $8.5 million sale of a 2023-built, 16-unit co-living property in West Los Angeles to UCLA Housing Group, who will convert it to student housing. The sale price of $531,250 per unit reflects distress in the co-living segment. The transaction closed via court-appointed receivership, signaling developer/sponsor losses on recent vintage product.
stories.impact: Co-living model failure in Los Angeles multifamily market signals that delivery of dense, amenity-light product no longer pencils absent strong rent growth to offset construction costs and carry costs. Expect continued contraction of new multifamily starts in LA as replacement costs remain elevated while achievable rents stagnate—creates window for selective land assembly but tightens underwriting on new development.

stories.title: Development Site with Uncommonly Long Frontage Sells in Brooklyn
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets closed the $23.5-million sale of 1150 Broadway, a residential development site in the Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn. The team of Brendan Maddigan, Steve Rutman, Mike Mazzara and Ethan Stanton represented the seller, A-PLUS International Realty, and negotiated directly with the buyers, Brooklyn-based YS Developers and Rabsky Group. Situated at the crossroads of Bedford-Stuyvesant and Bushwick, the 26,730-square-foot corner site is zoned for a mixed-use building with apartments, local retail and community facilities. Under the City of Yes for Housing Opportunity program, it offers up to 133,917 square feet of as-of-right zoning floor area. The property also sits within a federally designated Qualified Opportunity Zone and is eligible for the 485-x tax abatement program. The site features approximately 475 feet of wraparound frontage along Lafayette Avenue, Kosciuszko Street, Kossuth Place and Broadway. “Sites with this much frontage, this level of zoning flexibility and direct subway access rarely come to market in Brooklyn, and our marketing process generated significant interest from developers looking to establish a presence in the neighborhood,” said Maddigan. “YS Developers and Rabsky Group have a clear path to deliver a large-scale residential project with an attractive long-term position. The post Development Site with Uncommonly Long Frontage Sells in Brooklyn appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: YS Developers and Rabsky Group acquired 26,730 sq ft Bed-Stuy corner site for $23.5M.
As-of-right zoning yields 133,917 sq ft; 475 feet wraparound frontage; 485-x tax abatement eligible.
Qualified Opportunity Zone status and City of Yes zoning flexibility drive developer interest in outer Brooklyn.
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets closed a $23.5 million sale of a 26,730-square-foot development site in Bedford-Stuyvesant to YS Developers and Rabsky Group. The corner site offers up to 133,917 square feet of as-of-right zoning floor area for mixed-use (apartments, retail, community facilities), sits within a Qualified Opportunity Zone, and qualifies for the 485-x tax abatement program. The property features 475 feet of wraparound frontage and direct subway access.
stories.impact: City of Yes for Housing Opportunity zoning reforms and 485-x abatement eligibility are accelerating outer-borough (Bed-Stuy/Bushwick) development activity and reducing entitled zoning risk. Expect increased density and faster permitting in these submarkets, raising competition for land and tightening development margins. The QOZ benefit extends tax-advantaged capital availability through 2026, incentivizing sponsor equity deployment now.

stories.title: Triple-Net AutoZone Sells to Private Investor from LA
stories.excerpt: Hanley Investment Group Real Estate Advisors and Progressive Real Estate Partners arranged the $2.64-million sale of a renovated, single‑tenant AutoZone in Bakersfield. The building, originally constructed in 2013, underwent a full renovation in 2025 and is leased to AutoZone on a new 15‑year triple-net lease. EVP and partner Jeff Lefko and EVP Bill Asher of Hanley represented the seller, Torrey Financial Group, based in San Diego. The buyer, a private investor from Los Angeles, was represented by Greg Bedell, SVP and Managing Director, and Lance Mordachini, Vice President with Progressive Real Estate Partners in Rancho Cucamonga. “We procured an all‑cash, 1031-exchange buyer from Nevada,” said Lefko. “We negotiated a 40‑day escrow and closed at over 96% of the listing price, which reflects the continued depth of demand for essential retail in fast‑growing suburban markets.” Bedell added, “Our buyer was highly motivated and moved quickly because of the long‑term lease, the recent renovation, replaceable rent, and the investment grade strength of AutoZone. This asset checked every box for investors seeking stable, service‑based retail in supply‑constrained California markets.” The AutoZone is located at 1125 Olive Dr. in Bakersfield, occupying an 8,302‑square‑foot building. The post Triple-Net AutoZone Sells to Private Investor from LA appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Single-tenant AutoZone in Bakersfield sold for $2.64M on new 15-year net lease.
Building underwent full 2025 renovation; 96% of listing price achieved on 40-day escrow.
All-cash 1031-exchange buyer from LA/NV reflects sustained investor demand for essential retail in supply-constrained CA markets.
stories.summary: Hanley Investment Group arranged a $2.64 million sale of a 2013-built, fully renovated AutoZone in Bakersfield leased on a new 15-year triple-net agreement. An all-cash, 1031-exchange buyer from Los Angeles closed quickly at over 96% of list price on a 40-day escrow, citing the tenant's credit quality, recent renovation, and long lease term.
stories.impact: Limited impact to multifamily. However, continued strength in single-tenant retail investment reflects broader capital flight from multifamily and office into essential, non-discretionary retail—signals capital competition and potentially higher financing costs for multifamily development relative to yield-hungry industrial and retail debt.

stories.title: Northern NJ Industrial with Heavy Power Trades to Commerce Park Investors
stories.excerpt: Resource Realty of Northern New Jersey arranged the sale of a high-utility, standalone industrial facility located at 36 Pine St.in Rockaway, NJ. The transaction was brokered and finalized by firm Principals Greg Sabato and Scott Peck, who represented the buyer, Commerce Park Investors. The property encompasses 53,252 square feet of functional industrial space. Suitable for intensive manufacturing, assembly or specialized logistics, the building features heavy-duty infrastructure, including two tailboard exterior dock doors and one drive-in bay. Crucial for modern industrial users, the property boasts heavy power, equipped with a 2,500 amp, 440-volt electrical system capable of supporting heavy production loads. “This single-story property represents a unique opportunity for an operator requiring significant power infrastructure wrapped in a highly functional industrial footprint,” said Sabato. “Heavy power of this caliber – 2,500 amps – coupled with dedicated loading capabilities is an increasingly rare commodity in the northern New Jersey market. Securing this building underscores the sustained demand for spaces that can immediately accommodate a full-range of manufacturing and technical requirements.”  The post Northern NJ Industrial with Heavy Power Trades to Commerce Park Investors appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Commerce Park Investors acquired 53,252 sq ft high-utility industrial facility in Rockaway, NJ.
Heavy power infrastructure: 2,500 amp, 440-volt system; two dock doors and drive-in bay.
Northern NJ market sees rising scarcity of heavy-power industrial suitable for manufacturing and specialized logistics.
stories.summary: Resource Realty of Northern New Jersey brokered the sale of a 53,252-square-foot industrial facility at 36 Pine Street in Rockaway to Commerce Park Investors. The single-story property features heavy-duty infrastructure including a 2,500-amp, 440-volt electrical system, two tailboard dock doors, and one drive-in bay—capabilities increasingly scarce in the northern New Jersey market.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily. However, scarcity of heavy-power industrial in NJ reflects supply constraints and rising land/infrastructure costs in the region, which may elevate land acquisition costs for multifamily developers competing for development sites in northern NJ submarkets with similar zoning and utility constraints.

stories.title: Arrow Real Estate Advisors Hires Jeff Weinberg as Managing Director
stories.excerpt: Arrow Real Estate Advisors is adding another experienced veteran to its staff of capital markets experts. The New York-based real estate advisory firm has hired Jeffrey Weinberg as a managing director, Commercial Observer can first report. Weinberg comes from Meridian Capital Group, a firm he co-founded in 1991. Weinberg served as executive vice president, specializing in multifamily and office debt placement. “Jeff has built an exceptional career in commercial real estate and has an unparalleled depth of knowledge and relationships across the industry,” said Morris Betesh, founder of Arrow Real Estate Advisors. “His experience, judgment and entrepreneurial approach align perfectly with Arrow’s platform and culture.” Weinberg’s move is not uncommon. Betesh, previously a senior managing director at Meridian Capital Group, had exited the firm along with 12 team members to form his own capital markets advisory firm. Weinberg told CO that he joined Arrow Real Estate mainly due to the strength of his relationship with Betesh, whom he worked with at Meridian Capital Group for several years. “Morris and I were friends over there, we worked together at the old place, he left a couple of years ago, and I thought this would be a nice fit for me in this stage of life and my career,” said Weinberg. Weinberg was one of the original founding partners at Meridian Capital Group, where his expertise during a three-decade tenure ran from managing client and lender relationships to executing CRE transactions across developments and strategic relationships. He estimated that he has completed more than $1 billion in originations in his career. He told CO that he was attracted to Arrow Real Estate’s ongoing growth and expansion since the company was founded in October 2024. “I knew Morris had a very good team of professionals who know the market very well and I thought it would be a good fit to make my next move,” he said. bullets: Jeff Weinberg joins Arrow Real Estate Advisors as managing director from Meridian Capital Group.
Weinberg co-founded Meridian in 1991; specialized in multifamily and office debt placement.
Movement reflects ongoing consolidation and talent migration among capital markets advisory and debt placement firms.
stories.summary: Arrow Real Estate Advisors hired Jeffrey Weinberg as managing director; Weinberg previously served as executive vice president at Meridian Capital Group, which he co-founded in 1991, specializing in multifamily and office debt placement. Weinberg joined Arrow due to his relationship with founder Morris Betesh, who had previously departed Meridian with 12 team members to form Arrow.
stories.impact: Signals continued leadership churn and firm consolidation in debt placement and capital markets advisory—key intermediaries for multifamily development financing. Concentration of experienced multifamily debt placement talent at boutique firms may reduce transaction friction but could compress advisory fees and tighten lending discipline across the market.

stories.title: Alexandria Shows Positive Signs After Several Depressed Quarters: Earnings
stories.excerpt: Ailing Alexandria Real Estate Equities is showing signs of improvement as leasing increased over the second quarter of 2026, a hopeful sign of progress after several quarters of declining fundamentals. The life sciences-focused real estate investment trust (REIT) posted earnings Tuesday that show declining balance sheet performance with $73.7 million in net income for the second quarter of 2026 versus $109.6 million during the same period last year. Funds from operations (FFO) was $296.1 million, more than $100 million lighter than in the second quarter of 2025 and down a similar amount from the $396.4 million reported in the first quarter of 2026. Revenue declined from $762 million in the second quarter of last year to $662.7 million for the same period in 2026. Joel Marcus, Alexandria’s executive chairman and founder, however, was more optimistic than in previous quarters, stating that science sectors are improving economically, even if that progress has not yet been reflected on the real estate side. “We’re winning an outsized number of shares of transactions, which is good,” Marcus said during the call. “We have a very well-diversified and strong tenant base. … Very strong leasing in the second quarter from our life science products, service and device sector really depicts shovels and tools of the industry and is almost 40 percent of the leasing volume.” Alexandria leased 1 million square feet of space in the second quarter of 2026, compared to about 647,300 square feet in the first quarter, with about 329,000 square feet being deals that backfilled newly vacant space. In previous quarters, Alexandria executives have pursued dispositions to support the company financially while the life science market recovers. The company sold $170.3 million in assets, including 3825 and 3875 Fabian Way in Palo Alto, Calif., for $163 million in mid-July. bullets: Alexandria Real Estate (life sciences REIT) Q2 2026 FFO $296.1M, down $100M+ YoY.
Net income declined to $73.7M vs. $109.6M in Q2 2025; revenue fell $762M to $662.7M.
Life sciences sector improving economically, but real estate fundamentals lag; leasing activity rising.
stories.summary: Alexandria Real Estate Equities reported Q2 2026 earnings showing net income of $73.7 million (vs. $109.6 million in Q2 2025) and FFO of $296.1 million, down over $100 million year-over-year. Revenue declined from $762 million to $662.7 million. Despite balance sheet pressure, CEO Joel Marcus cited improving science sector economics and rising leasing activity as hopeful signs.
stories.impact: Tangential to multifamily; however, Alexandria's prolonged distress in life sciences real estate highlights sector-specific oversupply and capital exhaustion, which may redirect venture and institutional capital toward multifamily and logistics. If life sciences sector stabilization extends through 2026–2027, expect capital reallocation away from other asset classes and toward life sciences again, competing for multifamily development financing.

stories.title: Munish Viralam of Newmark: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Munish Viralam arrived at Newmark in June, fresh off an 18-year stint at CBRE. As executive vice chairman at Newmark, Viralam has been tasked with leading the firm’s newly centralized real estate strategy and consulting group, scaling up its strategic arm, and helping corporate tenants navigate the maze-like process of real estate strategy and negotiations. Viralam found his niche at Emory University, where degrees in finance and real estate placed him at an intriguing crossroads between the business world and entrepreneurship. He landed a job at CBRE after graduation, where he proceeded to spend nearly two decades honing his craft as a real estate strategist and problem solver. Viralam was serving as executive vice president in charge of CBRE’s consulting group in Manhattan when Newmark came a-knocking. Commercial Observer sat down with Viralam in July, just a few weeks into his tenure at Newmark, to discuss his vision for the group, New York’s office occupancy challenges and where real estate consulting slots into the dealmaking mix. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Can you describe the nature of the real estate strategy and consulting group’s work? Where does it fit into Newmark’s broader deal-making? Munish Viralam: We called it the real estate strategy and consulting group because we want to emphasize both of those components of what the practice is. It is a transactional-based group and it’s focused on advising large corporate entities within New York City on their real estate and occupancy strategies. It’s a pretty analytical approach, if you will, but that doesn’t just mean numbers. It means assessing all of the risks and the pros of strategies that we could pursue. The idea is to become a strategic hub for the organization. bullets: Munish Viralam joins Newmark as executive vice chairman after 18 years at CBRE.
Tasked with leading newly centralized real estate strategy and consulting group.
Reflects ongoing talent consolidation at major brokerage platforms competing for corporate tenant relationships.
stories.summary: Munish Viralam, formerly executive vice president of CBRE's consulting group in Manhattan, joined Newmark as executive vice chairman to lead the firm's newly centralized real estate strategy and consulting group. Viralam spent 18 years at CBRE honing expertise in corporate real estate strategy and tenant negotiations.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily. However, continued hiring and centralizing of corporate real estate strategy expertise at major brokerage platforms signals competitive intensity for large corporate tenant accounts—may reduce availability of senior broker talent for multifamily leasing and development advisory services.

stories.title: Prologis’ European Rival Segro Accepts $18.8B Takeover Offer
stories.excerpt: Prologis, the world’s largest industrial landlord, is about to get even bigger. The San Francisco-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has succeeded in its fourth offer to acquire rival Segro, the United Kingdom’s largest REIT, in a deal valuing Segro’s equity at roughly $18.8 billion. Prologis announced Tuesday that Segro’s once-resistant board would be recommending the deal. The combined portfolios’ global platform will total approximately $269 billion of assets under management. For the U.K., the deal means losing its largest REIT, the history of which stretches back more than a century. Segro’s portfolio spans approximately 117 million square feet across the U.K. and Europe, and has been made increasingly valuable by its expanding data center pipeline. “Prologis shares our conviction in the long-term structural drivers underpinning demand for modern logistics and data centre infrastructure,” David Sleath, CEO of Segro, said in a statement. “We believe the combination would bring together two highly complementary businesses and create a compelling platform, combining Segro’s exceptional portfolio and development pipeline with Prologis’ existing European business and global scale, customer franchise and operational capabilities, while retaining a shared commitment to disciplined capital allocation, customers and people,” Sleath added. Prologis’ European footprint is projected to grow by 47 percent with a 368 million-square-foot regional operating portfolio. The deal anticipates a combined European development pipeline of 13 million square feet and a 126 percent increase in Prologis’ European land bank. The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to legal, regulatory and Segro shareholder approvals. bullets: Prologis acquires Segro (UK's largest REIT) for $18.8B equity valuation on fourth offer.
Combined platform: $269B AUM; Segro portfolio spans 117M sq ft UK/Europe with expanding data center pipeline.
Consolidation of global industrial/logistics/data center platform under single operator.
stories.summary: Prologis successfully acquired Segro, the United Kingdom's largest REIT, in a deal valuing Segro's equity at approximately $18.8 billion. The combined portfolios will total approximately $269 billion in assets under management. Segro's 117-million-square-foot portfolio spanning the U.K. and Europe includes an expanding data center pipeline.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. This consolidation reflects mega-cap REIT capital deployment toward industrial/logistics/data center assets globally, signaling continued preference for these sectors over multifamily. Reduces number of institutional capital providers focused on multifamily, potentially tightening equity availability for development.

stories.title: Blue Owl’s Stack Infrastructure Buys Virginia Data Center Site for $66M
stories.excerpt: Blue Owl Capital is pushing beyond Northern Virginia’s Data Center Alley after acquiring a 71-acre development site in Culpeper, Va., for $66.4 million. Blue Owl’s data center operator Stack Infrastructure purchased Culpeper Technology Park at 15140 Keyser Road from RACM. The transaction is equal to more than $935,000 per acre. Greysteel arranged the sale for the seller and announced the deal Tuesday. The property is in the Culpeper Tech Zone, a county-designated data center corridor with significant power infrastructure and electrical capacity. The site has by-right zoning for data center development and access to multiple fiber networks. The zone also offers county tax incentives. Culpeper is about 60 miles southwest from the center of the world’s largest data center market. The competition for that hub has pushed developers and some of the nation’s biggest investment firms to expand into surrounding Virginia markets, especially as land, power and fiber capacity become more difficult to secure. “Culpeper has moved from a speculative secondary market to an institutional-grade destination in a short window,” Greysteel Senior Director Zach Benlemlih said in a statement. “The demand for entitled, power-proximate land in the Mid-Atlantic has only intensified as Northern Virginia supply tightens, and this transaction is a direct reflection of that.” Greysteel has completed seven transactions in Culpeper, including representing the seller when it originally acquired the technology park site, as well as other data center properties and land for industrial uses. “As primary markets price out all but the most liquid buyers, well-positioned secondary sites with entitled land, fiber and power access are commanding real institutional attention,” Lacey Willard, Greysteel’s executive vice president, said. bullets: Blue Owl's Stack Infrastructure purchased 71-acre data center site in Culpeper, VA for $66.4M ($935K/acre).
Culpeper Tech Zone: by-right data center zoning, significant power/fiber, county tax incentives.
Site ~60 miles from Northern VA Data Center Alley; reflects geographic expansion as core markets reach capacity constraints.
stories.summary: Blue Owl Capital's Stack Infrastructure acquired Culpeper Technology Park, a 71-acre development site in Culpeper, Virginia, for $66.4 million (approximately $935,000 per acre). The property is located in the Culpeper Tech Zone, which offers by-right zoning for data center development, significant power infrastructure, multiple fiber networks, and county tax incentives. Culpeper is approximately 60 miles southwest of Northern Virginia's core data center market.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily. However, mega-cap data center investment expanding into secondary tier-2 VA markets signals sustained capital reallocation toward infrastructure and away from residential. Rising land costs in secondary markets (data centers now commanding $900K+/acre in rural VA) may inflate land prices for all development types, compressing multifamily development feasibility in adjacent submarkets.
